post.originalText:
GPT-6 Astra built this hotel corridor inside Blender through MCP from 4 words.

No Sora, no Veo, no diffusion anywhere in the pipeline.

The prompt was "create hotel corridor scene," the model was gpt-6-astra on high, the bridge was Blender MCP with 28,500 stars on GitHub.

Then the terminal started writing Python.

Walls, sconces every 2 meters, a carpet pattern lifted straight off the Overlook then it rendered a test frame, saw the light bleeding wrong and moved the fixtures 3 times until the falloff sat right.

Nobody touched a mouse.

The geometry is real, so you can open the .blend, grab a vertex and drag it, and nothing in the frame is a guess about what a pixel should look like.

For 2 years the counterargument was that AI video can't hold a scene for 8 seconds without melting a door frame, which is true, so the model stopped generating video and started running the software instead.

GPT-6 Astra shipped September 4 at $10 per million tokens in and $50 out, with 1.1M context the whole Blender Python API and your scene graph in one window.

A junior 3D artist quotes $400 for a corridor like this and takes 2 days.

The render is clean, the lights land right, nobody opened Blender.
